profile.onboarding: No menu or tutorial; Level 1 opens straight into play with a controls panel (25 words: WASD/arrows, strafe, mouse look, touch drag zones) shown as an overlay the whole time. No taps required before play starts (taps-to-play check passed) but reading the controls text needs a 5-7 year old to be read to.
profile.controls: Keyboard W/↑ forward, S/↓ back, A/← strafe left, D/→ strafe right, mouse to look; touch play drags the left side of the screen to move and the right side to look, with no on-screen buttons.
profile.core_loop: Walk the 3D maze corridors, avoid the spike trap, and reach the exit door; touching the spike resets you to the start and you re-walk the path.
profile.goals_and_rewards: One goal per level: find the door. Winning shows "You found the way out!" with a "Play again" button; no stars, points, collectibles, or unlocks (bot run: kid persona 5-7 win rate 100% over 3 runs).
profile.difficulty_curve: Single 29x29-cell maze (perfect maze, 34-cell solution, 8 dead ends) with one spike hazard placed in a dead end only 3 cells from start, on-solution avoidable; fail cost is low (instant reset to start, 0-1 fails per kid run in the bot data) but there is no ramp beyond this one level.
profile.game_feel: Software-rendered fps averaged 37.6 (p95 frame 66.6ms, one spike to 466.6ms), no haptic/audio feedback on movement or the spike hit; solver bot finished near-optimally (99% of optimal path) while kid-persona runs bumped into walls often (11.5 bumps/min).
profile.art_and_audio: Low-poly pastel 3D (sky-blue walls, green floor, grey spike cone cluster, brown door with light-blue windows); 0 audio files, no speechSynthesis, no WebAudio — completely silent.
profile.session_length: Kid-persona (5-7) bot runs: median time to first win 53.95s, range 45-168s across 3 seeded runs, well within a 5-10 minute session; only one level exists so there's no continued session beyond that.
profile.usability: Automatic checks flag no in-play hint when stuck (idle 60s+ with no hint, target is ≤20s) and no visible pause/mute/quit controls on the playing screen (R16 fail); the persistent debug FPS/Position box is developer instrumentation with no value to a young player and adds visual clutter alongside the controls and level-name panels.
profile.accessibility: Text has good contrast (light text on dark boxes, brown/white "Play again" button) and hazards are shown by shape not color alone; but the controls text is a 25-word block above the 5-word max for this bracket, there is no spoken/audio version of any instruction (loudness check fails this bracket), and the page's meta-viewport disables pinch-zoom (axe moderate warning).
profile.ads_and_purchases: None seen; network check found only 2 same-origin requests and no analytics/tracker globals.
profile.notes: Biggest gaps for 5-7: missing pause/mute/quit control (fails rule R16), no audio/spoken instructions at all, and a text-heavy controls panel that a pre-reader can't parse alone — flagged by both the automatic checks and Claude's content review, despite play itself being fast, low-fail, and non-scary (spike is a simple grey cone, reset is instant).
